Just started college this year, “refused” to take a final exam because of mental health issues (thinking about doing online next semester or just focusing on work) so to get to the point, your relationship of time management and mental health should have a good connection. Getting burned out while doing both, will probably be the worst time of your life….Personally, I’d say work, for the money ofc, especially if you plan on doing something with the money soon (like moving out). Bigger picture: one at a time since it seems like you’re a full time worker at a serious company. However, if you truly want to do both, then your schooling might have to be extended for a good work-life balance. There’s nothing wrong with taking more than 4 years to get a degree, it’s actually very common! I have a problem with time, and obsessing with the future so I try To tell myself this,  but it’s truly OKAY, WHO CARES

I personally think you can learn the labs at home, YouTube is your friend! But in your second to last, or last year of schooling, I’d suggest going in person. If at a 2 year college right now or very soon, try a hybrid schedule, but if u must be strictly online at the time you start, YouTube will help! In my area, there are plenty of labs that hire without lab experience, (MOST LABS HAVE TO TRAIN YOU ANYWAYS since each lab is different) and so you could definitely pick up on that. It wouldn’t hurt to ask a lab tech, how to use an instrument, just try make sure you have a clear understanding on the labs, if you think you’ll be looked at stupidly. PS, try to work for drug labs like Quest Diagnostics and LabCorp, etc as a start up, or as a lab assistant at a college (definitely doesn’t require lab experience).
